title: Toyota Celica 1995 AC Pulley Repair: Pulley-Only Replacement, Shim Gaps, and Reassembly
summary: In this episode, The Car Care Nut examines a near-mint 1995 Toyota Celica Convertible with about 41,000 miles that is making an AC-related noise. Rather than replacing the entire compressor, he isolates the sound to the compressor pulley and demonstrates a pulley-only repair strategy. The process includes removing the compressor, bench-assembling and inspecting the clutch, explaining how the magnetic clutch works, measuring the clutch gap with a dial indicator, and selecting and installing shims to achieve the spec (~20 thousandths clearance). After validating the gap, he reinstalls the compressor, belts, and lines, charges the AC system, performs an oil and filter change on the 5S engine, and concludes with a tour of the car’s original condition and its maintenance history. The video blends diagnostic reasoning, careful parts selection in the face of scarce vintage parts, and practical, tool-based steps to service aging automotive hardware while preserving originality.
topics: belt inspection and original belt condition
spec clearance (20 thou) for clutch gap
belt tensioning by feel vs tool
oil and filter change on 5S engine
N1 vs F2 oil filter commentary

sections.title: Initial inspection and noise diagnosis
sections.description: The host introduces a 1995 Toyota Celica Convertible with ~40k miles, notes an audible noise, and frames the diagnostic objective around identifying the noise source before any parts are swapped.

sections.title: Pulley vs compressor: plan to replace only the pulley
sections.description: Discussion shows the nuisance part being discussed as the compressor pulley, not the compressor or clutch, due to scarce availability for the older compressor. The plan is to remove the compressor and replace only the pulley.

sections.title: Compressor removal and belt inspection
sections.description: The compressor is disconnected, evacuated, and removed from the car to access the pulley. The host notes the belt condition and that only the one belt needed for removal will be addressed.

sections.title: Disassembly of the clutch and pulley on the bench
sections.description: On the bench, the clutch, shims, and pulley are disassembled. The host discusses the goal of replacing only the bearing portion of the clutch and keeping the rest intact.

sections.title: AC clutch mechanics and part availability
concepts: how the clutch engages the compressor
sections.description: The host explains the magnetic clutch mechanism and shows how the inner hub, magnet, and belt-driven outer portion interact. He notes the one remaining available clutch part and discusses OEM vs aftermarket considerations.

sections.title: Clutch gap measurement and shim selection
sections.description: The video details the critical process of measuring the clearance between the clutch plate and the back of the pulley, using a fixed setup and a dial indicator. The host demonstrates adjusting the clearance with shims, tests different thicknesses (including one near center of the spec), and emphasizes accuracy over feel alone.

sections.title: Reassembly and initial installation of the pulley assembly
concepts: restoring the clutch assembly to the compressor
sections.description: With the correct shim stack chosen, the clutch/pulley assembly is reassembled and prepared for installation back on the compressor before reinstalling into the vehicle.

sections.title: Final installation, belt, and AC recharge considerations
sections.description: The host reinstalls the belt, discusses belt part numbers and potential supersession issues, initiates AC recharge, and begins a routine service step—an oil/filter change on the 5S engine—while noting the car's originality and the upcoming checks.

sections.title: Car evaluation, originality, and wrap-up
sections.description: The host tours the Celica, highlights its original exhaust and overall preservation, discusses related maintenance challenges with other cars in the shop, and ends with reflections on the car’s character and a plug to subscribe for future content.

featured_techniques.technique: Diagnosis: identify noise source as AC pulley rather than the compressor or clutch
Pulley-only replacement strategy for an older AC compressor
Bench disassembly of the compressor clutch and bearing inspection
Explanation of magnetic AC clutch operation
Dial indicator-based clutch gap measurement and zeroing approach
Shim-based adjustment to achieve spec clearance (~20 thou)
Reassembly with a new bolt and careful alignment before installation
AC system charging and post-repair checks paired with an oil/filter change on the 5S engine
